In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of the Higgs sector in models with an extended Higgs sector, in which there are more than one Higgs boson.
the study of top quark physics at hadron colliders and at linear electron positron colliders.
the study of the Higgs sector of the Standard Model and the search for new particles beyond the Standard Model at the Large Hadrons Collider at CERN (LHC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Higgs mechanism is the most successful model of particle physics ever.
the top quark is not a fundamental particle.
the Higgs bosons of the Standard Model (SM) and of the MSSM are indistinguishable at LHC, but the Higgs bosonic sector of the MSSM can be probed by the LHC and the ILC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the combination of measurements of tt̄H0 production at LHC and Higgs boson decays at the ILC can lead to a precise measurement of the top quarks Yukawa coupling in an almost model-independent way.

the Higgs bosons are not only a fundamental part of the standard model, but also play an important role in the physics of the early universe and in the formation of the large-scale structure of the universe.
we have shown how the Higgs bosons couplings to fermions can be extracted in a model independent way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of the LHC and ILS can lead to a precise determination of the top quarks Yukawa coupling, which is not possible with the LHC alone.
a measurement of the Yukawa coupling is possible in the near future, if the LHC and the ILC are combined.
